q.intro.text: Nia wants a copy of triangle A B C. She measures three parts: A B is seven inches, B C is five inches, and angle A is forty degrees. Then she builds a triangle with the same three parts. Must her triangle be congruent to triangle A B C? Pick one, and say how sure you are.

q.cb.yes.text: You said three matching parts always fix the triangle. The swing just showed two different triangles with the same three parts: the angle was not between the two sides.

q.cb.flip.text: You said it works unless she flips it. Flipping was never the problem: a flipped copy is congruent. The problem is that the same parts fit two different triangles.

q.cb.not.text: You said not necessarily, and the swing agrees: the same two sides and an angle that is not between them fit two different triangles.

e.intro.text: Which three parts are enough? Watch one criterion, S A S, from the marks to the proof. The picture moves first, then the line.

e.step0.text: Read only the marks. One tick: segment A B is congruent to segment D E. One arc: angle B is congruent to angle E. Two ticks: segment B C is congruent to segment E F. Three pairs, each with the reason: given. Nothing else counts, however it looks.

e.step1.text: Where does the angle sit? Angle B is the corner where A B and B C meet: it is included between them. Side, angle, side in a row: the pattern is S A S.

e.step2.text: Why is that enough? Flip a copy of triangle A B C over, as in a mirror: a reflection is a rigid motion. Slide B onto E. Turn about E until ray B A lies along ray E D: A lands on D, because A B is congruent to D E. Then the congruent angles put ray B C along ray E F, and the congruent sides put C on F. Every vertex has its own reason.

e.step3.text: Write the conclusion with matching vertices in matching places: A went to D, B to E, C to F. So triangle A B C is congruent to triangle D E F, by S A S. The motion works for every pair with these marks, not only this drawing.

e.why.text: Quick check: why must the angle sit between the two sides?

e.why.ok.text: Right. The included angle points the second side along the right ray. Its length then fixes the third vertex.

e.why.order.text: Not quite. The letters are not a mnemonic. Side, angle, side in a row means the angle sits between the two sides. That is what made each vertex land.

e.why.any.text: Not quite. With an angle that is not between the sides, the second side can swing to two different places. You will see it in Prove it.

t.intro.text: Your turn. A C and B D cross at E, and E is the midpoint of both. Prove that triangle A E B is congruent to triangle C E D. First put the lines in an order that works. Two of them are decoys. Then give each line its reason.

t.wrong.text: Not that one yet. Read the note under the proof.

t.order-done.text: The lines are in a working order. Now the reasons, top to bottom.

t.next.text: The triangles are congruent. What else do you now know, for free?

t.next.ok.text: Right: A B and C D sit in matching places of the congruence. Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are congruent. That is C P C T C.

t.next.corr.text: Not quite. A B matches the side of the other triangle in the same places: C D, not D E.

t.next.none.text: Not quite. Once the triangles are congruent, every pair of corresponding parts is congruent, marked or not.

p.intro.text: Back to Nia. Two sides and an angle that is not between them: S S A. Does it always fix the triangle?

p.build.text: Let us build it and see. For each line, pick the reason that makes it true. First line: C lies on the ray from A that makes forty degrees with A B, and on the circle of radius five inches about B.

p.build-test.text: Test it by building the triangle. For each line, pick the reason that makes it true. First line: C lies on the ray from A that makes forty degrees with A B, and on the circle of radius five inches about B.

p.c1.text: Right. Next line: there are two places for C.

p.c2.text: Right. Last line: S S A is not a congruence criterion.

p.c3.text: Same three parts, two different triangles. S S A is not a criterion.

p.x-flip.text: Not that one. Facing a different way never stops congruence. Look at the third sides.

p.x-ex.text: Not that one. One drawing that works proves nothing about every triangle.

p.x-other.text: True, but it is not the reason for this line. Read the line again.

p.claim1.text: C lies on the ray from A that makes forty degrees with A B, and on the circle of radius five inches about B.

p.claim2.text: There are two places for C.

p.claim3.text: S S A is not a congruence criterion.

p.hl.text: One change: make the given angle a right angle. A B is four inches, B C is five inches, and angle A is ninety degrees. How many triangles now?

p.hl.ok.text: Right. The circle meets the line at two points, mirror images across line A B, and only one of them is on the ray. One triangle. H L is a criterion.

p.hl.two.text: Look again. The second point is below line A B, on the far side of A, off the ray.

p.hl.none.text: Look again. The circle does reach the ray, once.

p.done.text: That is the whole story. S S S, S A S, A S A, A A S and H L fix a triangle. A A A and S S A do not.
